newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS END HIGHER ON NEW SHARES TRADING.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS END HIGHER ON NEW SHARES TRADING.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Friday with sentiment buoyed by the limit-up performance of microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor on the first trading day for its recent bonus issue shares, brokers said.
The weighted index opened higher and extended the rise for most of the session before closing 82.96 points or 0.84 percent higher at 9,923.84.
Turnover was moderate at T$151 billion.
The 1.427 billion new shares of Taiwan Semicon, issued during a June bonus issue, began trading on Friday and stimulated strong buying, brokers said.

Taiwan Semicon, the island's largest chipmaker, soared the daily seven-percent limit or T$10 to T$161. The electronic sector, which had been plagued by profit-taking in the past week, gained 3.21 percent to lead the market on Friday.
"The gains by Taiwan Semiconductor showed investors are very confident about the company's outlook," said Tsao Chung-ping, analyst for Ting Kong Securities.
"Since the company is a bellwether for the electronic sector, overall sentiment also was boosted," Tsao said.
Taiwan Semiconductor said on Wednesday it planned to speed up its proposed 10-year T$400 billion wafer project.
The overall market, in an extended electronics-led rally, has gained more than 40 percent in 1997. But it had suffered profit-taking in the three sessions before Friday.
Constructions, which had performed well despite the rest of the market's malaise before Friday, bucked the overall trend again and dropped 1.46 percent.
Heavily weighted financials fell 1.32 percent following interest rate hikes by several major commercial banks on Thursday that came after the central bank raised two key rates last week.
